subsystems.name: Space sensing layer
subsystems.role: global coverage where ground instruments cannot reach — oceans, ice, remote forest.
parts: radar satellites using interferometry to measure millimetre ground movement
atmospheric sounders for temperature, water vapour and greenhouse gases

subsystems.name: Ground sensing layer
subsystems.role: dense, high-precision measurement of the solid Earth beneath our feet.
parts: GNSS stations tracking slow crustal strain

subsystems.name: Ocean and ice layer
subsystems.role: the largest and least-instrumented part of the planet.
parts: drifting profiling floats measuring temperature and salinity with depth

subsystems.name: Biological sensing layer
subsystems.role: detects change in living systems, the hardest signals to automate.
parts: acoustic recorders and machine-learning birdsong or whale classifiers
environmental DNA water and soil sampling

subsystems.name: Quantum and precision sensing layer
subsystems.role: the frontier: instruments that measure gravity, magnetism and time far more sensitively than classical ones.
parts: atomic magnetometers for subsurface and volcanic imaging
optical atomic clocks for precise time and strain reference

subsystems.name: Communications and timing
subsystems.role: ties thousands of heterogeneous instruments into one coherent, timestamped record.
parts: low-power radio mesh between nearby nodes

subsystems.name: Data assimilation and AI
subsystems.role: turns a flood of raw readings into a running model of the whole planet.
parts: a digital twin for simulation and forecasting

buildSteps.title: Define the observables
buildSteps.detail: Decide what must be measured — ground displacement, soil moisture, seismic waves, species presence — and at what spatial spacing and how often, because this sets the whole cost.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Sensors must be calibrated to common references, report open, documented data formats, and carry metadata describing where and how each reading was taken. Without this, fusion is impossible.

buildSteps.title: Launch the space segment
buildSteps.detail: Constellations are built and launched in compatible orbital planes so the same patch of ground is imaged repeatedly, which is what lets radar interferometry detect slow deformation.

buildSteps.title: Deploy ground, ocean and biological networks
buildSteps.detail: Seismometers are installed in boreholes or vaults, floats are released on scheduled ocean cycles, and recorders, cameras and sampling sites are distributed by habitat type.

buildSteps.title: Connect and time-synchronise
buildSteps.detail: Each node is given power, a data link and a common clock, generally disciplined by satellite timing, so that a signal arriving at different stations can be triangulated.

buildSteps.title: Fuse into a digital twin
buildSteps.detail: Streaming observations are assimilated into a coupled model of the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere and biosphere, with machine learning filling gaps and flagging anomalies.

buildSteps.title: Validate and quantify uncertainty
buildSteps.detail: Each layer is cross-checked against independent instruments and past events, and error bars are published alongside the maps.

buildSteps.title: Deliver warnings and interfaces
buildSteps.detail: The system is wired into tsunami, earthquake, volcano and ecosystem alerting, where minutes of lead time matter more than any long-term trend.

prerequisites.why: instrumenting millions of points only makes sense if each node is cheap enough to leave unattended for years.

prerequisites.tech: Earth-observing satellite constellations with radar, gravity and hyperspectral payloads
prerequisites.why: space is the only practical way to get uniform global coverage, but revisit frequency and resolution are still limited.
cold-atom gravimeters and magnetometers exist in laboratories and early surveys, not yet as mass-deployed field stations.

prerequisites.tech: Global-scale data assimilation and machine learning
prerequisites.why: the computing and modelling techniques now exist but have not been applied across all these domains at once.

prerequisites.tech: Persistent power and connectivity in remote regions
prerequisites.why: satellite backhaul and solar-battery systems can already run isolated stations, though at a cost.

pathway.milestone: mature but separate observing systems: seismic networks, drifting ocean floats, weather satellites, biodiversity camera grids
pathway.unlocks: domain-specific science and hazard warnings, with little cross-talk between them.

pathway.milestone: national and regional digital twins of Earth, combining observations with physical models
pathway.unlocks: integrated simulation and forecasting over large regions.

pathway.milestone: field-deployable quantum gravity and magnetic sensors added to geophysical surveys and volcano monitoring
pathway.unlocks: seeing subsurface mass and fluid movement that classical instruments miss.

pathway.milestone: a genuinely federated global sensing and modelling layer with open data standards
pathway.unlocks: early warning of earthquakes, eruptions and ecosystem collapse as a shared public utility.

pathway.milestone: autonomous, self-organising sensor networks that reallocate coverage as anomalies appear
pathway.unlocks: a planet-scale feedback loop — the sense in which the idea is called a 'nervous system'.
